purpose: Trace benchmark findings through engineering decisions, releases and remaining debt; preserve evidence rather than search for favorable reruns.
claimBoundary: Published-source ancestry establishes inherited implementation, not unchanged behavior or newly measured 3.2 performance. Measurements remain bound to each campaign and exact source.

pre-effect.label: Pre-effect main in final client/adoption campaigns

adoption-selected.label: Selected B in ABBA adoption campaign

changes.title: Plain HTML for static native routes
changes.finding: The no-JavaScript benchmark page paid for adoption markers, row keys and empty island state.
changes.change: Omit adoption machinery only on native routes without JavaScript or islands; keep island contracts intact.
tradeoffs: Smaller bytes did not deliver the estimated 3,300/5,000 requests/s. Combined Sprint improved 3.74%; Endurance was 0.10% lower in this campaign.
remainingTargets: Investigate whole-request costs rather than treating removed bytes as a throughput prediction.
guardrails: Preserve visible content, CSP/response policy and strict adoption on island routes.
Do not relabel component measurements as a final 3.1 or 3.2 binary measurement.
repeatOnlyIf: A relevant compiler/static-renderer change or a preregistered whole-request hypothesis exists.

changes.title: Reduce native walker allocation and escaping cost
changes.finding: Profiling found temporary conversion/allocation costs in rendering; HTTP and walker-only clocks measure different work.
changes.change: Use reviewed allocation/escaping improvements while preserving emitted content and escaping security controls.
tradeoffs: HTTP marginal cost remained 11.006 ns/B; the walker-only target is not an HTTP claim. One Endurance tail-ratio sample reached 1.5264 although the frozen mean-based rule passed.
remainingTargets: Keep HTTP and walker clocks separate; profile data preparation/projection/transport for further gains.
guardrails: Keep exact nodes/list iterations, body parity, escaping mutant controls, and all outliers.
repeatOnlyIf: A measured walker path or a specific allocation hypothesis changes; do not rerun unchanged code for a nicer sample.

changes.title: Public-effect gains carry batching and own-engine gaps
changes.finding: Published public effects substantially lagged the exact engine used by Forma; comparisons to a different engine version were insufficient.
changes.change: Select the simpler supplied-node effect/lifecycle design with cleanup repair; retain pristine alien-signals 3.1.2 as a separate same-trial control.
tradeoffs: Batch throughput was 13.79% below published and 6.93% below pre-effect main. The 80% own-engine fan-out goal failed.
This campaign measures 9ac07a44; later RC3 observations are GP-H010 and supersede claims about the latest candidate.
remainingTargets: Reach at least 80% of the same-trial pristine engine for each effect workload without dropping lifecycle behavior.
guardrails: Keep synchronous updates, cleanup/disposal, reporting, owned subscriptions and all nine workloads.
Do not infer island-adoption gains from public-effect gains or aggregate away batching loss.
repeatOnlyIf: A scoped effect/batch design hypothesis has changed; retain exact own-engine version and all operations.

changes.title: Withdraw row optimizations that worsened real operations
changes.finding: The first qualified row candidate missed creation acceptance and slowed swap, removal and clear despite a smaller bundle.
changes.change: Withdraw unproven list changes in 16862984; retain their failed campaign and compare future proposals against the exact rejected design.
tradeoffs: A lower bundle size did not establish acceptable interaction speed. Fixed-order samples are bounded observations, not a universal causal effect.
remainingTargets: Create 1000 rows at no more than 1.10× same-trial vanilla remains the original target.
guardrails: Do not remove ownership/listener cleanup or reuse rejected generic-list code without a new reviewed contract.
Do not pool the failed and rollback VMs or select only favorable operations.
repeatOnlyIf: A materially different, explicit template/event or large-list strategy is preregistered with full correctness and cost coverage.

changes.title: Offer response compression as a deliberate opt-in
changes.finding: Rendered HTML was sent uncompressed while its marker-heavy output compressed well; per-request compression adds CPU and security costs.
changes.change: Add response-specific Brotli/gzip negotiation through with_compression; leave it off by default.
tradeoffs: Brotli reduced bytes by 92.5% but throughput by 26.0% and increased p99 by 34.2%. gzip also costs CPU/tail latency.
This pre-static executable does not predict the compression ratio of the final smaller static response.
remainingTargets: Choose compression only for an application workload whose transfer benefit justifies CPU, latency and response-security costs.
guardrails: Require response-specific BREACH review; preserve CSP/no-store/Vary and decoded-content correctness.
repeatOnlyIf: Response data shape, codec version/level, cache policy or deployment constraints materially change.

changes.title: Cache release dependencies before changing FMIR delivery
changes.finding: A page edit relinks the embedded Rust application; cold dependencies dominate uncached starter builds.
changes.change: Ship locked target caching in generated CI with read-only cache policy outside the default branch. Defer release FMIR-from-disk.

measurements.metric: Minimal Rust release cold → restored cache
Dashboard Rust release cold → restored cache

tradeoffs: One cold/warm pair per starter on separate runners is an example, not a distribution or guaranteed build speed.
Release disk-loading adds authentication, atomic-update and version-skew obligations; it was evaluated and deferred.
remainingTargets: Keep release build/deploy integrity while reducing repeat compilation work.
guardrails: Preserve exact lockfile/cache keys and default-branch write policy. Do not call skipped app recompilation an achieved optimization.
repeatOnlyIf: Cache keys/toolchains or starter workloads change; disk-loading work must first solve authenticated atomic deployment.

changes.title: Isolate tree-shaking gains from effect and row changes
changes.finding: Client-only apps retained unnecessary activation and development-related setup; combined candidates obscured attribution.
changes.change: Extract the bundle-only change and measure identical app/dependency builds independently of rejected rows and public effects.
tradeoffs: The isolated 237 B Brotli gain is not the later integrated app size; effect/ownership/compiler changes add separate costs.
Mapped-module byte totals come from another build; compression savings are not additive by module.
remainingTargets: Keep unused features out of the measured client-only import graph without weakening ownership APIs.
guardrails: Retain exact app, dependency, bundler and source hashes; keep static byte results separate from timing campaigns.
repeatOnlyIf: Reachable import graph, package splitting or emitted production code changes.

changes.title: Keep initial adoption cost separate from public effects
changes.finding: Public-effect improvements did not establish adoption performance; strict adoption uses the raw engine.
changes.change: Run a fixed ABBA 1000-binding regression control and explicitly accept the measured adoption cost.
tradeoffs: Mean adoption rose 0.3400 ms (3.96%); both B-leg means exceeded both A legs. No-adoption-regression was not demonstrated.
One 7.1 ms A update drives the lower update mean; medians 1.0 → 1.1 ms do not support a clean speedup. Historical error capture was narrower than current harness requirements.
remainingTargets: Improve adoption while retaining zero initial writes and node identity; do not promise equality from overlapping spreads.
guardrails: Keep every leg, five warmups/15 samples per leg, existing update/disposal checks and explicit source binding.
repeatOnlyIf: Adoption path or its emitted graph changes, or a preregistered model warrants a new ABBA control.

changes.title: Adopt compiler-created rows only as explicit opt-in
changes.finding: Generic row construction remained a weakness; early literal/fresh-event prototypes were insufficient and unsafe to promote broadly.
changes.change: Ship reviewed clientTemplates:true for eligible client-created rows, with staged evaluation, delegated callbacks and guaranteed cleanup; default stays off.
tradeoffs: Clear cost rose 22.17% (+0.94 ms); select/swap also rose. Creation remains above 1.10× vanilla.
The package graph cap was explicitly raised 49,414 → 49,926 gzip B; unchanged route budgets still reject oversized opted-in native fixtures. Adopted lists do not receive this clone path.
remainingTargets: Improve client-created rows without expanding compiler semantics silently or removing cleanup.
guardrails: Keep option default-off, unsupported-shape refusals, staged expression order, raw-sink policy and stale-callback revocation.
Preserve route/startup limits; a package cap increase is not permission to increase route budgets.
repeatOnlyIf: A scoped compiler design or shared-chunk packaging hypothesis changes; compare all nine operations and actual opted-in delivery bytes.

changes.title: Startup repair leaves later client regression debt visible
changes.finding: RC3 startup qualification failed source-bound 57.260/60.373 ms tasks; later byte-equivalent DOM programs still showed adverse timing observations.
changes.change: Enable eager compilation hints for five private adoption functions without changing bodies or startup bounds; accept bounded client costs explicitly.

evidence.label: RC3 startup repair and current client costs

tradeoffs: Same-campaign current vs 8ae throughput changes: fan-out −13.11%, diamond −11.29%, effect creation −8.79%. Published-relative gains do not erase these losses.
Current app is 773 B Brotli above published 3.0. The original fan-out, effect-create and row targets remain missed.
Separate failed and repaired startup campaigns do not form a same-host speed comparison. Byte-identical APIs do not prove compilation, module-layout or collection causes.
remainingTargets: Reach >=80% own-engine fan-out and effect creation and <=1.10× same-trial vanilla creation; retain the 50 ms startup engineering target.
guardrails: Retain every sample/control, startup source binding, unchanged ownership and size gates; do not rerun solely for favorable values.
The bounded 55 ms exception policy is explicit, not a replacement for the 50 ms target or a retroactive pass.
repeatOnlyIf: Relevant source/emitted graph or a preregistered mechanism changes; otherwise reuse the accepted evidence with exact applicability proof.

changes.title: Qualify transport and preserve rejected campaign evidence
changes.finding: Probe/load user agents differed; twelve React Router samples had unresolved body-size discrepancies. Original rankings were not qualified.
changes.change: Use identical explicit request headers, retain probe bodies and full load-generator output, and run a separate corrected campaign instead of patching historical numbers.
tradeoffs: Aggregate byte equality and retained probes do not prove the content of each timed response. Hosted VMs do not prove exclusive physical hosts.
Historical unresolved/failed runs stay excluded; changing a harness validator does not upgrade old evidence.
remainingTargets: Preserve fair controlled comparisons and explicit qualification boundaries as adapters evolve.
guardrails: Use same-campaign ratios and exact lock/source/browser/resource identities; never pool unrelated VMs or crown an overall winner.
Memory <=8 MiB, readiness remainder <=50 ms and image <=150,000,000 B remain source-specific strength guards.
repeatOnlyIf: Headers, transport, dependency/runtime versions, workloads or resource profiles change; replay retained evidence before spending a new race.

changes.title: Carry 3.1 lessons into 3.2 without inventing a rerace
changes.finding: Benchmark-driven improvements shipped in 3.1 and are inherited by 3.2; router release qualification has different clocks and scopes.
changes.change: Record release ancestry, current packed decoder observations and explicit timing/soak waivers separately from Grand Prix measurements.
tradeoffs: The accepted decoder bound was 30.7 ms but actual tagged p95s also passed original 30 ms. This is not a decoder speedup comparison.
Additional 20-run N7 campaign and one-hour soak were explicitly waived; 577 s is one observation, not p95. Outer release target missed.
No fresh full Grand Prix campaign for exact stable 3.2 is established by these release documents. Inherited code is not inherited timing identity.
remainingTargets: Use a new versioned same-host race when a changed measured path needs evaluation; do not repeat waived release work or claim it passed.
guardrails: Keep security/correctness, cleanup and archive provenance mandatory; preserve original failed reports and decisions.
Do not compare 3.2 decoder/CI observations to older Grand Prix clocks.
repeatOnlyIf: A specific 3.2-or-later change needs measured attribution under a frozen campaign; otherwise retain exact release/evidence boundaries.
